small_guidance:
- The conv kernel's inner loop over (IC, KD, KH, KW) = (3,3,3,3) = 27 mults per output is small; try unrolling by flattening the IC*KD*KH*KW loop and preloading the 27 weights into registers per (oc) program once, instead of loading w_val inside the innermost loop on every od iteration. Hoist weight loads outside the od loop.
- Add larger BLOCK_HW configs that better cover OHW=900 (e.g. BLOCK_HW=900 rounded to 1024 with num_warps=8/16, num_stages=2) and try a 2D tiling (oh_tile × ow_tile) so KH/KW shared input rows can be reused via shifted loads.
- Reorder loops so od is innermost and reuse the input column across od (since id_ = od+kd shares (KD-1) planes between adjacent od values) — keep a rolling window of partial sums per kd-plane to cut input loads ~3x.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, OC_tile, OHW_tile), with K = IC*KD*KH*KW = 81 fully unrolled, and fuse the min-over-OD reduction as an epilogue that loops od and keeps a running min of the GEMM result. Use tl.dot on BLOCK_M (OC) × BLOCK_K (81) × BLOCK_N (OHW tile) for tensor-core throughput.
- Alternatively, since OD=22 is the reduction axis and OC=24 is small, make one program compute a full (OC=24, OHW_tile) tile and fuse conv+min+softmax in a single kernel: after computing min per (n, oc, hw) tile, immediately do channel softmax across OC in registers (OC fits in one warp tile), eliminating the second kernel and the out_min round-trip to HBM.
- Exploit depth-axis reuse: for a fixed (n, oh_tile, ow_tile), load each input depth-plane once and accumulate partial conv contributions into all OD outputs it touches (scatter-style along od), then min-reduce — this turns the D×H×W input read from O(OD) reads into O(1) reads per element.
